validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/ATTRIBUTION/STATUS all confirmed. FERC Docket No. CP16-493-000 (Columbia Gas Transmission, L.L.C.) is titled the 'Central Virginia Connector Project' in three published Federal Register notices (NOI to prep EA 2016-10-03; Notice of Application 2016-08-31; Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review 2017-01-18) — this matches GEM's SegmentName almost verbatim and is FERC's/the applicant's own official project name, not a GEM invention. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (federal statistical agency; independent of FERC/Federal Register) carries 'Central Virginia Connector' as Project Name, Operator 'Columbia Gas Transmission', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2018-09-04, Year In Service 2018, State VA/VA, Additional Capacity 45 MMcf/d, Pipeline Type Interstate, Authority FERC, Docket Number CP16-493 — identical between the Jan-2020 and Aug-2026 releases of the workbook (record stable/unchanged since 2018). The FERC notices independently confirm: facilities located in Louisa and Goochland Counties, Virginia (supports StartState/Province=Virginia, EndState/Province=Virginia); 'the increase in HP will provide an additional capacity of 45 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d)' (supports Capacity=45.00 MMcf/d); classification as an interstate natural gas transmission facility regulated by FERC (supports Fuel=Gas, PipelineType). Owner1='Columbia Gas Transmission LLC' 100% is confirmed as both the FERC applicant/filer of record and the EIA-listed Pipeline Operator Name — no other owner/operator named in any source read. CAVEAT: gem.wiki's own Columbia_Gas_Transmission page (read for leads only, never cited) does NOT use the string 'Central Virginia Connector' anywhere; it describes numerically-identical data (Operator=Columbia Gas Transmission, Owner=TC Energy, Capacity=45 MMcf/d, Length=0 new km, Status=Operating, Start Year=2018) under a different prose section header, 'Virginia Expansion Project' — this is an editorial/descriptive label choice by the wiki editor, not evidence GEM's SegmentName is wrong; FERC and EIA both independently use 'Central Virginia Connector' as the official project name. Also confirmed NOT a duplicate/collision with gem.wiki's separate, unrelated 'Virginia Electrification Project' (VEP) entry (350 MMcf/d claimed on wiki vs. TC Energy's own now-dead VEP page, recovered via Wayback snapshot 20240117221105, stating 35 MMcf/d, Petersburg Compressor Station, construction expected 2023, in-service late 2023) — VEP is a materially later, differently-scoped, differently-located project from P2516's 2016-filed/2018-completed Louisa/Goochland facilities; no roster PID among the 46-row Appalachian gas duplicate-check list was identified as VEP's GEM entry, so no cross_row_lead is filed for it (VEP does not appear to be tracked in this batch's scope). Checked and found IRRELEVANT to P2516: the pdigm.com PDF citation (dead, 404 as of 2026-09-08) and the Ohio PUC document citation (Northern Loop Pipeline Project is a Columbia Gas of Ohio distribution-system project, unrelated to this Virginia interstate segment); also checked a Virginian-Pilot article about a 2023 pipeline explosion, which occurred near I-81 in Shenandoah County, VA — a different county from P2516's Louisa/Goochland facilities, so not this project.

validity.recommendation: Update LengthKnown from 0.00 km to ~0.19 km (0.12 mi) and fill Diameter=8 in — this project is not a pure compression-only expansion; FERC's own Notice of Application states new pipe was installed.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current LengthKnown=0.00 km appears to follow the standing SOP convention 'expansion with no new physical pipe -> LengthKnown=0', but that convention does not fit this project: FERC's Notice of Application (Docket CP16-493-000, filed Aug. 12, 2016) states the project will '(iv) install 0.12 mile of 8-inch-diameter pipeline' at the Louisa Compressor Station, alongside the compressor/horsepower upgrade (replacing three Solar Saturn units with one Solar Centaur 50, increasing HP from 4,050 to 6,130) and a new meter station at the Goochland Compressor Station. 0.12 mile = 0.19312 km (x1.609344), proposed as 0.19 km. This is a single-origin finding (Federal Register/FERC) for the specific 0.12-mile/8-inch figure — the EIA workbook's Miles and Pipeline Diameter (Inches) fields for this exact record are both blank (None), so EIA does not corroborate or contradict the length/diameter figures; a second, independent corroborating source was searched for (WebSearch budget exhausted this session; DuckDuckGo HTML/Lite both blocked by anti-bot CAPTCHA challenges; Bing returned decoy/generic dictionary-definition results consistent with anti-scraping detection; FERC eLibrary is an Angular SPA behind Cloudflare not curlable without fabricating an API call) but none was found. Recommend medium-tier confidence on the exact 0.12/8-inch figures pending a second source, but HIGH confidence that LengthKnown=0.00/blank Diameter is wrong as a classification of this project (FERC's own filing explicitly describes new pipe being installed, contradicting the 'no new physical pipe' premise).
